tldr_label: TL;DR — Americans vote tomorrow as Trump weighs Iran strikes after the midterms; Israel's president opens coalition talks this week

tldr_bullets.label: US
tldr_bullets.body: Trump made his final rally stops in Iowa and Kansas, where Senate seats are close. A New York Times/Siena poll found Democrats ahead in all seven battleground states. [[TAG:info:vote Tuesday]]

tldr_bullets.label: Iran
tldr_bullets.body: Iranian negotiators left talks in Doha with a draft proposal circulating. Trump says the war will end 'one way or the other', and strikes after the midterms remain possible. [[TAG:danger:strikes possible]]

tldr_bullets.label: Israel
tldr_bullets.body: The election commission says the results stand despite Netanyahu's claim of a 'stolen' vote. Reports say the Arab parties will back Eisenkot when Herzog's consultations begin on Wednesday.

tldr_bullets.label: Ukraine
tldr_bullets.body: The Oleshky truce has expired after evacuations, and Russian strikes left hundreds of thousands of homes without power.

tldr_bullets.label: Europe
tldr_bullets.body: Poland's court standoff between Tusk and Nawrocki escalated. In Bulgaria, Iliana Iotova won the presidential runoff on a platform of talks with Russia.

tldr_bullets.label: Markets
tldr_bullets.body: US futures rebounded after last week's tech sell-off. Apple and Palantir report after today's close, and Brent eased toward $111.

sections.title: America Votes
sections.summary: Trump makes his final push in Iowa and Kansas as polls show Democrats ahead

paragraphs.heading: Final rallies
paragraphs.body: Al Jazeera reported that Trump held rallies in Dubuque, Iowa, and Salina, Kansas, on Sunday to defend the Republican Senate majority. One poll it cited had Democrat Adam Hamilton leading Senator Roger Marshall 49% to 44% in Kansas. In Iowa, Democrat Josh Turek led Ashley Hinson 48% to 47%. Yahoo News said Trump pitched voters on the economy. [[TAG:warning:toss-ups]]

paragraphs.heading: Final polls
paragraphs.body: Newsweek reported that Democrats gained in the polls before Election Day. Al Jazeera, citing a New York Times/Siena poll, said Democrats lead in all seven battleground states. Senate control depends on close races in Michigan, Texas, Kansas, Iowa, North Carolina and Alaska. These are polls, not results. [[TAG:info:polls only]]

sections.title: Iran After Doha
sections.summary: Iranian negotiators leave Doha with a draft in circulation; Trump weighs strikes after Tuesday

paragraphs.heading: Talks
paragraphs.body: The Jerusalem Post reported that Iran and Qatar held a third day of talks as fears of renewed US strikes grew. Arab News said Iranian negotiators then left Doha, but an official said the talks were not derailed and that a draft proposal is circulating. Tehran says a seven-step plan to reopen Hormuz and end the US naval blockade could be carried out faster under a deal. Reports differ on whether contacts are continuing. [[TAG:warning:status unclear]]

paragraphs.heading: Strike threat
paragraphs.body: CBS News reported that Trump said the war will be 'put away very soon, one way or the other'. The Media Line reported that Trump is weighing renewed strikes after the midterms. He has said he will not attack before Tuesday's vote but has not ruled out action afterward.

sections.title: Israel's Mandate Race
sections.summary: Officials say results stand; Arab parties reportedly back Eisenkot as Herzog's talks near

paragraphs.heading: Results stand
paragraphs.body: Al Jazeera and PBS reported that Israeli officials say the results will stand despite Netanyahu's claim that the election was 'stolen'. PBS said the suspects in the related bribery case were released. NBC News reported that President Herzog urged parties to engage with an 'open heart' to avoid another election. His consultations are set to begin on Wednesday.

paragraphs.heading: Eisenkot's numbers
paragraphs.body: News Beep reported that the Joint List and Ra'am are expected to recommend Eisenkot for prime minister. Combined with his own bloc, that would give him 67 recommendations. Eisenkot has previously ruled out a coalition that includes the Arab parties, so whether he could govern with their backing is unresolved. [[TAG:warning:unconfirmed]]

paragraphs.heading: Somaliland
paragraphs.body: Ynet and i24NEWS reported that Israel's first ambassador to Somaliland, Michael Lotem, presented his credentials in Hargeisa and laid a cornerstone for an embassy. allAfrica covered the move from the Somali side. Somalia has disputed Israel's recognition of Somaliland.

paragraphs.heading: Gaza
paragraphs.body: Al Jazeera, citing hospital sources, reported that Israeli attacks killed at least eight Palestinians across Gaza on Sunday, including five police officers in al-Mawasi. The Israeli army said it targeted 'a terrorist'. Al Jazeera said more than 1,500 people have been killed since last October's ceasefire. [[TAG:danger:8 killed]]

sections.title: Ukraine
sections.summary: Oleshky truce expires after evacuations as strikes hit power grids on both sides

paragraphs.heading: Truce ends
paragraphs.body: NBC News and CBC reported that civilians evacuated from Oleshky during the local ceasefire reached Ukrainian territory by way of Russia and Belarus. Vatican News said Pope Leo welcomed the truce, which expired on November 1. Evacuation counts differ: some reports say hundreds left, and US statements cited nearly 800. Ukrainian officials said about 1,700 people remain. [[TAG:warning:counts differ]]

paragraphs.heading: Strikes
paragraphs.body: NBC News reported that Russian strikes cut power to hundreds of thousands of Ukrainian households despite Trump's push for an energy ceasefire. ABC News (Australia) reported that Russia opened a terrorism case over a Ukrainian strike on an industrial site in Nizhny Novgorod region.

sections.title: Europe
sections.summary: Poland's court fight between Tusk and Nawrocki escalates; Bulgaria elects Iotova

paragraphs.heading: Poland
paragraphs.body: CNN reported that a long-running dispute between pro-European Prime Minister Donald Tusk and pro-Trump President Karol Nawrocki over the Constitutional Tribunal escalated after the court's president was suspended and police blocked its entrance. Al Jazeera said Nawrocki held crisis talks, which Tusk's party boycotted. US News reported that Tusk vowed to support the tribunal's independence. [[TAG:warning:constitutional crisis]]

paragraphs.heading: Bulgaria
paragraphs.body: Reuters, via Internazionale, reported that near-final results show acting president Iliana Iotova won the presidential runoff. She becomes Bulgaria's first elected female president. Balkan Insight said she has pledged a reset with Russia. Euronews reported that her rival conceded. Official results are due in the coming days.

sections.title: Africa and Asia
sections.summary: South Africa's local vote tests the ANC; Nigeria's suspected Ebola cases test negative

paragraphs.heading: South Africa
paragraphs.body: The Washington Post reported that South Africans vote in local elections on Wednesday in what is seen as a tough test for the ruling ANC. Daily Maverick said polls differ, with some putting the ANC and the opposition DA both near 30% and Johannesburg as the key battleground. The electoral commission says polls open at 7 a.m. [[TAG:info:vote Wednesday]]

paragraphs.heading: Ebola in Nigeria
paragraphs.body: Voice of Nigeria reported that Nigeria's disease control agency said two suspected Ebola cases in Adamawa State tested negative after two rounds of tests. A case in the capital territory remains Nigeria's only confirmed infection. Tribune Online had earlier reported the two suspected cases in the north-east.

paragraphs.heading: China
paragraphs.body: Digg, citing reports, said China's central bank planned a Monday meeting with regulators and major banks on supporting the stock market. Investinglive said a private manufacturing PMI was due after weak official data released on Saturday.

sections.title: Markets Week Ahead
sections.summary: Futures bounce after the tech rout; Apple and Palantir report as oil eases

paragraphs.heading: Futures and Asia
paragraphs.body: CNBC reported that US stock futures rebounded ahead of a busy week of earnings, economic data and the midterms. Saxo and Kaohoon reported mixed trading in Asia, with figures varying by source. Brent fell more than 2% toward $111 a barrel, as reported by World Today News. [[TAG:success:futures up]]

paragraphs.heading: Earnings
paragraphs.body: TipRanks and EBC reported that Apple is expected to post revenue of about $113 billion, with gross margin the key figure to watch. It will be CEO John Ternus's first earnings call. TipRanks said expectations for Palantir are high after a strong run in its shares. Both report after Monday's close, Benzinga noted.
